stories.headline: Padres rout Cubs 8-0 in emphatic Wild Card opener with Tatis' leadoff homer, King's no-hit bid
stories.summary: — Fernando Tatis Jr. hit the first leadoff homer in Padres playoff history on the Cubs’ first pitch, Michael King took a no-hitter into the seventh...
stories.body:
SAN DIEGO -- — Fernando Tatis Jr. hit the first leadoff homer in Padres playoff history on the Cubs’ first pitch, Michael King took a no-hitter into the seventh inning and San Diego rolled to an 8-0 victory over Chicago in their NL Wild Card Series opener on Tuesday night.


Manny Machado also homered in the first inning and added an RBI double in the third during an emphatic opening statement by the 91-win Padres. Xander Bogaerts also homered off Cubs starter Matthew Boyd, and Jackson Merrill added a two-run single later.


San Diego provided more than enough support for King, who struck out eight over seven stellar innings while thoroughly throttling the majors' highest-scoring team. King set the tone by striking out probable NL MVP Pete Crow-Armstrong with the first three pitches.


“It gives me confidence knowing the team has confidence in me to pitch in these games,” King said. “But then when you have our superstars showing out like that in the bottom of the first, it makes it a lot easier.”


Nico Hoerner got the Cubs’ only hit off King with a one-out infield single in the seventh, but King racked up two more strikeouts to earn the last of several standing ovations from the raucous sellout crowd watching his third career playoff start.


“The crowd was awesome,” Chicago manager Craig Counsell said. “They had a lot to cheer about tonight, and we didn't give them anything to be quiet about.”


Game 2 is Wednesday night at Petco Park. The series winner faces the MLB-best Milwaukee Brewers in the best-of-five division series.


Chicago had just one hit before getting to Joe Musgrove, the Padres veteran making his first major league appearance since Oct. 2, 2024, in the ninth inning. The Cubs got two singles and a walk before Musgrove struck out pinch-hitter Michael Conforto to preserve the shutout in his return from Tommy John surgery.


The Padres dominated the opener of this rematch of last fall’s Wild Card Series, won by the Cubs in three tight games. San Diego scored more runs in the first five innings of this series opener than it did last year in all three games at Wrigley Field combined.


When asked if his postseason managerial debut could have gone any better, San Diego's Craig Stammen replied: “No, probably not."


“We couldn't write it up any better ... (but) it's just one game, and we've got a job to do to finish the series off," Stammen added. "The Cubs are a great team. They didn't play their best game tonight, but I guarantee they're going to play their best game tomorrow.”


San Diego finished this season with the majors’ sixth-best record, besting Chicago by two wins and setting franchise records with its third straight playoff berth and fifth straight winning record. The Padres hit the postseason on a 17-3 roll, and they’re still surging.


Boyd’s opening pitch was a changeup, and Tatis crushed it 405 feet to center in a blast reminiscent of his first-inning homer in Game 1 of San Diego’s 2024 NL Wild Card Series victory over Atlanta.


Moments later, Machado smashed another changeup out to left-center, setting off pandemonium at Petco with his franchise-record ninth postseason homer.


“Honestly, it was hard to stay locked in in the bottom of the first,” King said with a smile. “I love to celebrate my guys hitting homers, but obviously I have a job to do. Hard to stay dialed in on what I was doing because it was an absolutely electric atmosphere.”


Tatis walked in the third and scored from first on Machado’s double to the wall. Bogaerts connected in the fourth, lining a full-count changeup into the seats on the Western Metal Supply Co. building above left field.


“When those guys are leading the charge, we're a pretty tough team,” Stammen said.


San Diego loaded the bases in the fifth against reliever Javier Assad, and Merrill cracked a two-run single to center before Ty France scored on a passed ball.


King escaped the minor trouble he faced, picking up key strikeouts and throwing his sweeper superbly. Hoerner got Chicago’s hit on a grounder that Machado stopped with difficulty, but couldn’t transfer to his throwing hand cleanly enough to make a play.


Tatis scored his third run in the seventh when he singled, stole second and ran all the way home when the throw trickled into center. Tatis slid headfirst past the tag and came up screaming while Machado theatrically signaled him safe.


Up next
Nick Pivetta (3-2, 2.86 ERA) starts Game 2 for the Padres in his fifth game back from a near five-month absence with a right elbow injury. Kevin Gausman (4-2, 4.83) goes for the Cubs.

stories.headline: WNBA playoffs 2026: How the Liberty swept the Lynx and the Fever stayed alive
stories.summary: New York eliminated No. 1 seed Minnesota while No. 6 seed Indiana held court vs. Las Vegas to stay alive.
stories.body:
The Indiana Fever fought off elimination. The top-seeded Minnesota Lynx weren't as fortunate.

Indiana, playing at home at Gainbridge Fieldhouse, beat the No. 3 seed Las Vegas Aces 99-89 on Tuesday, forcing their first-round series of the 2026 WNBA playoffs back to Las Vegas for Game 3 on Thursday.

But the No. 8 seed New York Liberty eliminated the Lynx in Tuesday's nightcap. After stealing Game 1 in Minnesota on Sunday, the Liberty ran over the Lynx 87-71 at Barclays Center. New York is the first 8-seed to knock off a No. 1 seed.

Jonquel Jones and Breanna Stewart each had 21 points and Sabrina Ionescu added 18 for the Liberty, who became the first team to advance to the WNBA semifinals. Lynx guard Olivia Miles, unanimously named WNBA Rookie of the Year on Monday, finished with five points.

In Indiana, Caitlin Clark finished with 27 points, 15 assists and seven rebounds, despite fouling out with 2 minutes, 45 seconds remaining and the Fever up 92-83. She shot 9-for-18 from the field and 5-for-11 on 3-pointers. Kelsey Mitchell added 26 points and Aliyah Boston 22.

Jackie Young led Las Vegas with 31 points, while MVP front-runner A'ja Wilson had 22 points and nine rebounds.

ESPN was courtside for all the action. Here's how both games were won.

JUMP TO: How the Liberty won | How the Fever won | Relive Tuesday's action

(8) New York Liberty 87, (1) Minnesota Lynx 71

How the game was won: New York players spoke before the game about having fresh in their minds how they, in Stewart's words, got "smoked" at home in Game 2 of last year's first-round series before dropping the decisive Game 3 in Phoenix. The Liberty played with an urgency from the tip on Tuesday, suggesting they fully understood they couldn't let that happen again. They jumped to an early 10-point lead, and even though Minnesota hung around, it never felt like they completely lost the control of the game. It was an all-around complete performance from the Liberty, who got huge nights from Sabrina Ionescu (18 points, seven assists) and Jonquel Jones (21 points, 13 rebounds) after Breanna Stewart carried the team in Game 1. Though Stewart wasn't too shabby herself, finishing with 21 points, five rebounds and four assists on the night.

What it means for New York: After a 13-12 start to the season and ending up with the No. 8 seed, the Liberty advance to the semifinals, keeping them in the hunt for their second championship in three years. They showed why they could never be viewed as a true eight seed in the playoffs. Minnesota only led for 3 minutes and 23 seconds this series, all of which were in Game 1.

What it means for Minnesota: A third straight heartbreaking playoff finish for the Lynx, who became the first No. 1 seed in WNBA playoff history to be swept in their opening series. Hard to imagine this won't result in some real questions internally in Minnesota as the Lynx collapse in epic fashion now two years in a row. -- Alexa Philippou

Breaking down how Minnesota was eliminated

What happened to the Lynx?

Kendra Andrews: Overnight, the team that sat atop the WNBA standings throughout the majority of the regular season looked like a shell of itself through both first-round games. Olivia Miles missed the last two games of the regular season with a calf injury, and she admitted to being nervous in Game 1 -- her playoff debut. But the unanimous Rookie of the Year scored just two points in the first game and five on Tuesday (she also sat for the final six minutes of the game).

A rookie is going to be inexperienced in these types of moments, but it doesn't explain what happened to the veterans. The Lynx were hopeful Napheesa Collier would hit her peak by the start of the postseason. Instead, she looked uncomfortable, combining for 26 points in the two losses. Kayla McBride scored 14 in both matches, and Courtney Williams had just nine points in Game 1. Simply put, as soon as the playoffs started, the Lynx lost all the spark that made them so dangerous for the past four months.

What was the biggest factor in the 1-seed being eliminated?

Andrews: The Liberty are no ordinary 8-seed. And lucky for them, their championship experience got the job done against the Lynx. In Game 1, Breanna Stewart proved why she is one of the best winners in women's basketball, finishing with 34 points and 12 rebounds. In Game 2, the Liberty's big three -- Stewart, Sabrina Ionescu and Jonquel Jones -- took over. For as much inconsistency and identity searching New York had to do under first-year head coach Chris DeMarco, both games of the first round looked like vintage Liberty basketball.

Their takedown of the Lynx in Game 2 was surgical and was a gentle reminder of how good this core is, but also what playoff experience -- and championship experience -- can accomplish on this stage.

Meanwhile, Minnesota looked disjointed. Collier, McBride and Williams have competed together at the highest level but didn't look like it at key moments. After Game 1, Lynx coach Cheryl Reeve challenged Collier to be more assertive -- something a coach doesn't want to have to urge their star player to do in the playoffs. New York knew exactly what it needed to do to not let Game 2 get away from it and allow the series to head back to Minnesota.

Minnesota-New York by the numbers
Courtesy of ESPN Research

The Minnesota Lynx are the first 1-seed in WNBA history to be swept in their opening series.

This is the first time that Minnesota has lost consecutive games by 15 or more points since a two-game streak between Sept. 10-13, 2023. This is the Lynx's first time losing consecutive playoff games by 15 or more points.

Minnesota's 16-point elimination loss is the third worst in franchise history.

Minnesota led for just 3 minutes, 23 seconds this entire series -- those leads came in Game 1.

The New York Liberty have won their past five playoff games when leading by 10 or more points at the half. The last time they lost despite a 10-plus point lead was Sept. 27, 2025, against the Indiana Fever.

Conversely, the Lynx are now 3-11 all-time in playoffs when trailing by 10 or more points at the half.

Liberty rookie Pauline Astier had a huge defensive impact on the floor in Game 2: Minnesota was just 4-for-19 (21%) when she was the primary defender.

The Liberty took full advantage of open looks throughout this series: They were 30-for-46 from the field (65%) and 14-for-27 from 3 (52%).

New York's Breanna Stewart, Jonquel Jones and Sabrina Ionescu together scored or assisted on 70 points. The Lynx had 71 points as a team.

Stewart now has 31 career 20-point playoff games, third most in WNBA history behind Diana Taurasi (44) and A'ja Wilson (33).

(6) Indiana Fever 99, (3) Las Vegas Aces 89

How the Fever stopped the Aces' high-powered offense: The Fever defense showed up Tuesday night. As a unit, the Fever seemed a split-second quicker than Las Vegas. They double-teamed more often than in Game 1. They cut off diving lanes. Help defense seemed to be in the right spots consistently. Nothing came easy inside, particularly for A'ja Wilson, who wasn't quite as decisive with the ball as she was Sunday. Also, shots that fell for Vegas in Game 1 clanked away in Game 2. Those Chelsea Gray fadeaways from the elbow weren't hitting. Jackie Young didn't seem to have her touch, though she ended up finishing with a game-high 31 points. After a 26-point first quarter, the Aces cooled as an entire team. Once again, nothing came easy, particularly in the half court, like so much did in Game 1. -- Kareem Copeland

What went wrong for the Aces: Wilson wasn't really herself for a lot of the game, and credit goes to the Fever defense. It's ultra-rare for Wilson to not even take a shot in a quarter, but that's what happened in the third period. Wilson's frustration showed in the fourth quarter when she was assessed a technical foul in a confrontation with a fan behind the basket. Wilson still finished with 22 points and nine rebounds. The Aces defense wasn't as strong as it was in Game 1, either, as the Fever shot 52% from the field. Overall, it wasn't the same Aces team as the one that had won its last eight games. -- Michael Voepel

What are the keys to Game 3? The Fever played much better defense in Game 2, and that made a difference in their offense, too. The Aces shot 59% from the field and scored 102 points in Sunday's Game 1, which was not much of a contest. But from the start Tuesday, the Fever were locked in defensively and were able to keep Wilson in check for key stretches of the game. A lot of her 22 points came while the Aces were trying to rally. Indiana didn't let that happen.

And while Young hurt the Fever with 31 points, the overall defensive job by Indiana was very good. Now, the Fever have to try to repeat that Thursday, which won't be easy. But at least they know the formula.

"It's always starting in practice -- that's all they talk about, 'Defense, defense, defense,'" said Fever rookie guard Raven Johnson, who played nearly 22 minutes off the bench, of the Indiana coaches.

Johnson said they especially emphasized "low I" defense, which is when two defenders on the weak side can help protect the paint and the passing lanes.

"I feel when we go back to film, they'll be very proud of us," Johnson said. "Everybody was on it. We were scrambling." -- Voepel

This series has been all about which team has the mightier triumvirate. The Aces' combination of Wilson, Gray and Young were so in sync in Game 1 that they made everything look easy. Wilson was decisive with the basketball and quick into her actions. On the other end, she looked like the best defensive player on the planet. Gray ran the offense with precision and buried those timely fadeaways that have become her trademark. Young's 21 points came on just 14 shots, and she handed out 10 assists. The trio combined for 93 of the Aces' 102 points. On Tuesday, they combined for 63 points on 15-for-41 shooting.

Things went in reverse for the Fever. Clark and Mitchell were held to 10-for-33 shooting in Game 1 as neither looked particularly comfortable. Boston shook off her recent slump with 18 points as Indiana's brightest spot Sunday. All that changed Sunday as Clark (27 points, 15 assists) became the first player in league history to record 25 points and 15 rebounds. Mitchell scored 26 and Boston added 22 as the team shot 52.1% as a whole. These two teams are built similarly with a dynamic backcourt and a No. 1 pick at center out of South Carolina. Both teams will go as far as their big three takes them. -- Copeland

stories.headline: Kessler talks up Lakers' title hopes behind 'nasty' defense
stories.summary: New addition Walker Kessler is convinced the Lakers have the right guys to be "a nasty defensive team" and a contender in the Western Conference this season.
stories.body:
EL SEGUNDO, Calif. -- The Los Angeles Lakers' offense has thrived since Luka Doncic arrived in 2025, but center Walker Kessler needed only one day of training camp to be convinced the team's defense will hold up its end of the bargain this season.

"Listen, I think we're going to be a nasty defensive team," Kessler said Tuesday. "I think people aren't taking into account how good our perimeter defense is going to be. A lot of guys are very smart on the perimeter and positionally can play really good defense. We have guys who are just ball hawks."

During JJ Redick's two seasons as coach, the Lakers have ranked above average in offensive efficiency and below average in defensive efficiency. After a transformative summer that saw the departure of LeBron James and several other veteran players, the Lakers are hoping to establish a more aggressive defensive identity with a rebuilt roster that includes Doncic, guard Austin Reaves, Kessler and a deep group of young wings.

Redick said Tuesday that his first goal during training camp was to "establish our defensive principles." With both forward spots in the starting lineup open for competition, Redick said he met with the team's wings last week to give them their marching orders.

"They understood the assignment today," he said. "That was exciting. They set the tone for us defensively. There was a lot of physicality, a lot of grabbing and holding, and a lot of disruption without gambling."

The 7-foot-2 Kessler, who was traded by the Utah Jazz to the Lakers this summer, will serve as the back-line rim protector after averaging 2.4 blocks per game during his first four seasons.

"The paint is kind of closed when [Kessler] is on the court," Doncic said.

From there, Doncic's remade supporting cast includes defensive specialists Jarred Vanderbilt and Matisse Thybulle as well as free agent additions Quentin Grimes, Sandro Mamukelashvili, Collin Sexton and Ziaire Williams. Kevon Looney, a veteran center who won two championships with the Golden State Warriors, will back up Kessler.

Kessler praised Looney for his "mind and positioning," Vanderbilt for his skill defending all five positions, and Thybulle, Grimes, Sexton and Williams for their ability to apply defensive pressure.

"Having those guys that can steal the ball ... [and] when they do get beat, be able to recover, it makes my job a lot easier," he said. "It's a lot easier to block a shot when a dude has someone on his hip instead of an open lane towards the basket."

The Lakers boasted the NBA's No. 3 defense when they won the 2020 championship and the No. 1 defense during the 2020-21 regular season. But their performance on that end has slipped noticeably in the years that followed.

Los Angeles fired Frank Vogel as coach after ranking 21st in defense during the 2021-22 season, then fired his successor, Darvin Ham, after ranking 17th in defense in 2023-24. The Lakers finished 20th on defense last season, their first full campaign after trading All-Star big man Anthony Davis to the Dallas Mavericks for Doncic.

Kessler was confident the Lakers "definitely can be a contender" in a Western Conference that includes title favorites with elite defenses such as the Oklahoma City Thunder and San Antonio Spurs.

"I think we have a lot of great tools and versatility," he said. "The guys are already getting along. Connection makes championship teams."

stories.headline: Cowboys' Schottenheimer 'aligned' with Jones after Rio gaffes
stories.summary: Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer said he would "be better" after meeting with Jerry Jones about questionable late-game coaching decisions in Sunday's loss to the Ravens.
stories.body:
FRISCO, Texas -- Dallas Cowboys owner and general manager Jerry Jones did not mask disappointment with the decisions made in the final 28 seconds of Sunday's loss to the Baltimore Ravens in the NFL's first game in Rio de Janeiro.

Jones and coach Brian Schottenheimer went through the end-of-game decisions, from the playcalling after the Cowboys faced first-and-goal from the 2, to Dak Prescott's third-down throwaway that led to a tying field goal, to how the subsequent kickoff and seven seconds were handled, allowing the Ravens to kick a winning field goal with a second to play.

"There is no explanation you're satisfied with. None," Jones said on 105.3 The Fan in Dallas on Tuesday morning. "Let's be sure that we all understand that. [The coaches] don't have one that they're satisfied with. ... But there's an evaluation of how not to make the same mistakes again. You can't get that back. [There's] no way to get it back. What you can do is use it ... to get better. That's what's being done."

Schottenheimer accepted responsibility with Jones and publicly in his first comments after the team's return from Brazil.

"I'm man enough to take mistakes. I make a lot of mistakes. I'm certainly not perfect," Schottenheimer said. "And I know one thing, Jerry and I had a very good conversation about it. I explained it. He understands. He understands that there was a mistake that was made, and he was terrific. Great, sound advice. I value him. He's been around the game a long time, just like I have, and he's seen a lot of stuff.

"And so to me, that shows that he and I are aligned very closely. This will make me better. I'll be better. And again, I'm looking forward to lining up and playing this week against the Texans."

Schottenheimer added, "I hurt our chance to win that game and I'll be better. And I'm better than that. I'm better than I performed in the last 28 seconds."

After the game, Schottenheimer said he "overcoached" Prescott on the third-down pass to George Pickens that was a throwaway.

"I trust Dak Prescott completely, so it was the word that I chose, which I'm not going to give away," Schottenheimer said. "The words that we say have meaning, and when I said the word, it put him into a mindset that he doesn't play with. He doesn't play that way. He doesn't play the game that way. And so that's what I would change."

After Brandon Aubrey tied the score with a 23-yard field goal, the Cowboys had him kick the ball through the end zone for a touchback. The Ravens took over at their own 35, and quarterback Lamar Jackson hit receiver Zay Flowers for a 27-yard completion to set up the 56-yard kick from Tyler Loop with one second left.

In retrospect, Aubrey's kickoff should have been short to burn time off the clock.

Schottenheimer said his emotions of the third-down call affected the kickoff decision, adding that the communication between special teams coordinator Nick Sorensen and game management coordinator Ryan Feder was not good enough either.

"My dad had a rule -- one play at a time," he said, referring to former NFL coach Marty Schottenheimer. "He talked a lot about it, because it happened to him. He made a decision on a play, it didn't go good, he was pissed off about it and it affected another decision. I think that's kind of what happened to me. So I'll take accountability for it. It's football and life. It's what happens."

As he did after the game, Schottenheimer did not express regret over defensive coordinator Christian Parker's call that allowed the completion to Flowers.

"I think the coverage was OK," he said. "We played way too tight, and there was an error on that play where we should have made the ball go to the low underneath guy, not the deep one."

Schottenheimer has been a head coach for only 20 games, although he is in his 25th year in the NFL. Parker, 34, is a first-time coordinator. So far, the defense has not performed consistently, but Jones said he remained confident in what his team could accomplish this season.

Injuries have hit the defense with safety Jalen Thompson (hamstring) probably headed to injured reserve with a designation to return. Schottenheimer said defensive tackle Jonathan Bullard could sit out a couple of weeks because of a calf strain. The Cowboys could see safety Malik Hooker (forearm) and linebacker DeMarvion Overshown return this week against Houston, but the team worked out five players, including former Cowboys safety Juanyeh Thomas and Bengals linebacker Germaine Pratt.

The Cowboys' next three opponents -- the Texans, Tampa Bay Buccaneers and Green Bay Packers -- have one win combined this season. The New York Giants lost quarterback Jaxson Dart for the season to a knee injury, and Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels is out because of an elbow injury sustained against Dallas.

"We are very much in the hunt, and I say that principally based upon the way I feel about our team, as much or more than what's happening with the other teams," Jones told The Fan on Tuesday. "Philadelphia has things that they want to work on just as the Giants do, just as we do. It makes you see how health is a factor. Availability is a factor. And we're just getting started."

stories.headline: AFL player movement tracker: trade requests, free agency latest, who's on the move?
stories.summary: The offseason is upon us which means AFL trades, free agency, and player movement is about to take off. Here's the latest news, whispers, and confirmed deals.
stories.body:
It's AFL player movement season, with trades and free agency set to dominate the month of October. So who is going where? Keep track with our player movement guide here.

When is the AFL trade and free agency window?
The 2026 AFL trade period commences on Monday, October 5 and closes in the evening of Wednesday, October 14.

The free agency window opens and closes a little ealier; it runs from Friday, October 2 until Friday, October 9.

Tuesday, Sept. 29
Neale informs Lions he intends to join Collingwood

Two-time Brownlow Medal winner Lachie Neale has told Brisbane he will depart the club as an unrestricted free agent and sign a three-year deal with Collingwood.

Aware that Neale intended to leave at the end of the year, the Lions never offered him a new contract.

The paperwork for the deal is expected to be formalised as early as Friday when the free agency period opens.

Friday, Sept. 25
Jordon Butts to join the Bulldogs

Zak Butters isn't the only South Australian-based player keen to join the Western Bulldogs, with Crows' key defender Jordon Butts officially naming the Dogs as his preferred offseason destination.

The unrestricted free agent will sign a five-year deal at the Kennel, according to AFL.com.au.

Tuesday, Sept. 22
Amartey officially names Carlton

Wantaway Sydney forward Joel Amartey has confirmed his desire to join Carlton as an unrestricted free agent.

The 26-year-old was kept out of the Swans' side with an Achilles injury in the latter stages of the year.

With Charlie Curnow (75 goals in 2026) and Logan McDonald (51) cementing their spots in the Sydney forward line as the prime targets, Amartey is hoping for more opportunity at the Blues.

Thursday, Sept. 17
GWS captain finally makes big call on his future

Toby Greene has opted to leave GWS, telling the AFL club he wishes to play with Geelong next season. Greene, who has been at the Giants since their foundation season in 2012, wants to go back to Victoria for family reasons.

In an extraordinary way to announce the decision, outgoing GWS boss Dave Matthews confirmed Greene's intentions on radio, before the club released a statement.

The 32-year-old has been offered a lucrative three-year deal to join the Cats.

Saturday, Sept. 12
Zak Butters makes huge free agency call
The year's hottest restricted free agent Zak Butters has made a huge call on his future, nominating the Western Bulldogs as his preferred destination.

After a year of speculation, with Geelong thought to be the front-runner for the Power star's signature, Butters made the call on Saturday, first reported by AFL.com.au's Callum Twomey.

The deal is reportedly for nine years.

Thursday, Sept. 10
Hogan set to join Pies
GWS and Collingwood have both confirmed that 2024 Coleman Medal winner Jesse Hogan has chosen the Magpies at his next home.

Set to be a four-club player, Hogan is 31 and coming off a 12-goal season from just nine appearances.

It's a big boost for the Magpies if Hogan can recapture his form; key forward has been an area of concern for a number of years.

Tuesday, Sept. 8
Bailey set to be Lion for life
Brisbane's Zac Bailey has ended months of 'will he, won't he' speculation to sign with the Lions for eight years, taking him through the 2034 season, the the club confirmed on Tuesday.

Bailey, a free agent, had been a big target for the Crows, who had reportedly tabled a more lucrative offer.

"I'm absolutely rapt to be staying at the Brisbane Lions," Bailey said in a statement.

"I love the environment here, the players, coaches and staff who all make it a great place to be and I feel like this Club continues to bring the best out of me.

"This Club means so much to me - I came here as a young player and have grown up here and to know I will be here long-term is something I'm really proud of.

"I would like to thank the club, my partner Em, my family and my management for being so supportive throughout this process.

"I love what we as a club have achieved during my time here and I am super excited about what we can continue to achieve together."

Rowan Marshall requests trade
St Kilda ruck Rowan Marshall looks set to be on the move, with the Saints confirming the big man had requested a trade for the second straight season.

While Marshall hasn't requested a specific club, it's likely to be Geelong after he failed to secure a trade to the Cats last year. He played 21 games for the Saints this seaosn, juggling ruck duties with Tom De Koning, who came in from Carlton last offseason.

"Rowan is a highly valued member of the St Kilda Football Club and remains contracted until the end of 2027," the Saints said in a statement.

"Marshall has not nominated a preferred destination at this stage, with the club making clear that any trade will need to be in the best interests of the St Kilda Football Club."

Zane Duursma wants to go to Melbourne
The No. 4 pick in the 2023 AFL draft Zane Duursma has requested a trade out of North Melbourne, with Melbourne in his sights.

The news comes a week after coach Alastair Clarkson was sacked by the club. North won nine games in 2026, their best return since 2019.

Ed Allan re-signs with the Pies
After speculation about his future at the Magpies, mdifielder Ed Allan has put pen to paper, signing a four year extension to remain at Collingwood.

2026 was a breakout season for Allan, who played 19 games and averaged a career-high 16.5 disposals per game.

Monday, Sept. 7
Pair of in-demand Dogs re-sign
According to afl.com.au, both Arty Jones and Buku Khamis will remain at the Kennel this offseason.

Jones will sign a three-year deal, while Khamis has a five-year contract in front of him.

Essendon and Brisbane had interest in livewire forward Jones, who had a standout performance against Collingwood in the wildcard final win, while the Blues were heavily linked to Khamis for a second straight offseason.

Cooper Hodge nomintes Hawthorn
A big boost for the Hawks, with club champion Luke Hodge's son Cooper choosing to join the Melbourne-based team as a father-son at this year's draft.

He had the option of going to Brisbane as a Lions academy member.

stories.headline: Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy: Man City verdict could lead to Premier League expulsion
stories.summary: Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy has said Manchester City could be thrown out of the Premier League after being found guilty of all charges of financial breaches by an independent commission.
stories.body:
Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy has said Manchester City could be thrown out of the Premier League after being found guilty of all charges of financial breaches by an independent commission.

The league has said City breached its financial rules on a huge scale between 2009-10 and 2017-18 after arranging 'sham' commercial deals as part of a disguised funding scheme.

Nandy told Channel 5 News: "I don't want to preempt any kind of appeal process, and they are entitled to a fair hearing. But what I would say is that the ultimate sanction is very serious indeed.

"I mean, a club can be expelled from the Premier League if these sorts of allegations are upheld, with obviously huge repercussions for everybody.

"So there are very serious sanctions, and I think the bigger issue is how do we make sure that we have clearly understood rules that are upheld and applied consistently, and that we can move quickly when they're breached.

"The Premier League is one of our greatest exports. It brings joy to millions of people, and we want to make sure that we protect it for the fans for the future."

Former City chairman David Bernstein said the league's findings were "damning beyond belief" and that "the sanctions cannot just be financial".

Bernstein, who spent five years in the role before stepping down in 2003, also suggested the club's board should "be suspended immediately."

He told BBC Radio 5 Live: "It is damning beyond belief. My immediate thoughts are, should the board continue? Should the people involved be suspended immediately?

"Very, very serious. I think it's really terrible. There's a school of thought with lawyers that is 'deny, deny, deny', but this is a football club that is part of a league and the whole credibility of the league is at stake here.

- Man City learned of guilty verdicts in summer before transfer activity - sources

- Man City CEO adamant legal battle with the Premier League is not over - reports

- Marcotti: Hard to see how Man City recover from extraordinary guilty verdict

"I would go as far [as to say it is a deep-seated form of fraud] and if it is, I'm not a lawyer but as a thought this is something so serious that it goes beyond the football authorities.

"The sanctions cannot just be financial, so it's got to be way beyond that. If the appeal fails, Manchester City cannot stay in the league, they have to suffer. And I say that as a supporter and a fan."

Football finance expert Kieran Maguire says City's breaches have "gone far beyond the worst-case scenario that anybody initially envisaged."

Maguire told BBC Radio 5 Live: "If you Google what the word 'sham' means, I'm getting the words 'fake, false, fraud'. It's very, very significant.

"I think the quantity of money involved -- [approximately] £900 million over a nine-year period -- is a staggering misstatement, and it looks like it's been a corroborative fraud.

"The fact that the auditors were unaware of it, there must be collusion at the club.

"I think it's gone far beyond the worst-case scenario that anybody initially envisaged."

City have confirmed their intention to appeal, stating the commission's decision "contains clear material errors, of law, principle and fact, and is unsafe."

When asked on what grounds City could launch an appeal, Maguire added: "I've spoken to some sports lawyers today, just in case this did arise, and the consensus that I had coming back was that it's difficult but not impossible for Manchester City to say that ultimately this is some form of commercial dispute between two entities and therefore it should be taken away from the football authorities and dealt with [by] the standard legal courts in the country."

"Blue Moon" podcast host and City fan David Mooney said he had been "taken aback" by the scale of the league's findings.

"I don't think there's a word in the English language that covers how damning this is," Mooney told BBC Radio 5 Live.

Mooney said it was "a really dark day to be a City fan" and when asked about possible sanctions, he added: "The book needs to be thrown at the club.

"Ultimately, if they're not successful on appeal, they've lied to the fans throughout all of this, they've lied to the football bodies. They've lied to everybody.

"So, what is an adequate punishment? I don't know."

Former Manchester United captain Roy Keane said if he was a City player he would throw all the medals in the bin.

He said on ITV: "They knew it would hurt a lot of people, but they've still done it, and if I was a player I'd be 100% sticking those medals in the bin.

"It's cheating. You're hearing nonsense about some ex-players saying 'oh well they won on the pitch'. Because it was cheating! It was cheating going on."

stories.headline: PSG chief Al-Khelaifi has 'zero interest' in FIFA presidency
stories.summary: European soccer's search for a candidate to challenge Gianni Infantino in the FIFA presidential election will not land on clubs' leader Nasser Al-Khelaifi.
stories.body:
GENEVA -- European soccer's search for a candidate to challenge Gianni Infantino in the FIFA presidential election will not land on clubs' leader Nasser Al-Khelaifi, the Paris Saint-Germain boss insisted Tuesday.

Al-Khelaifi also is chairman of the influential European Football Clubs group and so sits on the executive committee of UEFA, which is leading efforts to oust Infantino after his failed plan to sell stakes in future World Cup profits to private investors.

- Will anyone stop Infantino? FIFA president is confident U20 World Cup cameo says otherwise

- FIFA agrees in principle to federation payments from WC windfall

- FIFA accuses UEFA of 'misinformation campaign' over World Cup proposal

As a minister in the government of 2022 World Cup host Qatar -- which has so far supported Infantino -- Al-Khelaifi also could have broad appeal to FIFA voters in Asia, yet he moved to quash speculation he might try to lead soccer's governing body.

"I have zero interest in FIFA, zero agenda [or] ambition to be there," Al-Khelaifi said at a news conference after an EFC annual meeting in the Danish capital Copenhagen.

"I don't think I'm the right guy for this position and I don't want to go actually, I'm enjoying what I'm doing," the president of Champions League title holders PSG said. "I think FIFA's not for me. Thank you."

The annual meeting of the 900-member club was held amid a volatile time for soccer politics and Infantino's future.

It is two months after Infantino's multi-billion dollar FIFA subsidiary plan was revealed, then defeated within days, and seven weeks before the deadline for candidates to challenge him.

UEFA president Aleksander Ceferin is leading the campaign to end Infantino's presidency either before or at the March 18 election in Morocco, and he spoke to club leaders Tuesday.

"Football has no need for emperors," Ceferin said in a near 10-minute speech that did not name Infantino, whose biggest plans since his first election in 2016 have typically been seen as threats by his former employers at UEFA.

Ceferin's references, including creating an award for a politician, were clearly aimed at Infantino and his close working relations with U.S. President Donald Trump.

"It's time to say enough," said Ceferin, a FIFA vice president who has ruled himself out of being a candidate. "Rules bent when inconvenient. Those meant to have a say simply cut out. And football's future treated as just another bargaining chip."

Ceferin, like Infantino, was elected in 2016 -- in the fallout of FIFA's previous biggest crisis, provoked by U.S. and Swiss federal investigations -- and also can seek a fourth and final term in office next year.

"Football needs great leaders like you," Al-Khelaifi said of Ceferin in his own speech, adding "we ask you to stand for president again next year."

Ceferin, who said in 2024 he would leave office in 2027, is likely to be unopposed in the UEFA vote by 55 member federations scheduled in April in Astana, Kazakhstan.

stories.headline: Ferrari gives Fred Vasseur 'full confidence' amid Christian Horner speculation
stories.summary: Ferrari has insisted it has "full confidence" in Fred Vasseur amid mounting speculation about both his job and the potential of Christian Horner replacing him.
stories.body:
Ferrari has insisted it has "full confidence" in Fred Vasseur amid mounting speculation about both his job and the potential of Christian Horner replacing him.

In a hastily-arranged virtual news conference on Tuesday, Ferrari's chief communication officer Maria Conti said the team -- under-pressure due to poor results on the track -- wanted to avoid any "gossip" moving forwards.

"We have confidence -- full confidence -- in Fred Vasseur and in his team, and we continue to do so," she said. "At this time it's really important that the team remains united and cohesive, and we are focused with all the energy on the work ahead.

"Ferrari has always attracted extraordinary interest, and it's only natural that many professionals aspire to be part of it. It is a reflection of the strength of what Ferrari really represents.

"So, this is why we really want to avoid, and we do not intend to fuel speculation or comment on assumptions coming from outside the company.

"And it's not just related to the story in the times of Mr. Horner, but in general, the speculation about Fred."

An interview Horner had given The Times, published ahead of last weekend's Azerbaijan Grand Prix, took on a life of its own ahead of the Baku event. Horner's interview, which had been primarily to promote his new autobiography, out next month, included a response to a question about whether he would take the Ferrari job.

Horner replied: "Would I consider Ferrari? I mean, Ferrari is the biggest brand in Formula 1. It's the dream. And arguably it's the sleeping giant of Formula 1."

Sources have told ESPN the former Red Bull boss was not intending to use the Times interview to declare his interest in Vasseur's job, and that he is not actively pursuing a job with the Italian job as things stand, nor has he been offered one. Either way, the quote dominated the build-up and aftermath of the Baku race.

After Saturday's event, a frustrated Vasseur said he had been asked "25 times a day" about his job and the Horner link.

The speculation around Vasseur and Ferrari leadership has reached fever pitch recently as the team's performances have slumped.

Earlier this month, Lewis Hamilton posted to Instagram to deny multiple reports in Italy that he was pushing for changes to be made to senior members of the race team -- the seven-time world champion said he still backed Vasseur after the Baku race.

Tuesday's press conference comes ahead of a race in Malaysia -- F1 is in the middle of the first of three triple headers (nine races across 11 weekends) to close out the season Conti added that while news about Ferrari is not uncommon, it was time to draw a line in the sand underneath it so the team can focus on the remainder of the season.

- Lando Norris apologises to Franco Colapinto after calling for ban

- Russell's win won't kick-start title challenge, but Baku rewards his faith in trying 2026

- Charles Leclerc admits Ferrari's rivals have taken 'big steps forwards': 'We must not lie to ourselves'

"We are doing that today, on Tuesday 29th of September, because we would like to avoid that the next weekend in Malaysia will be focused only on this kind of gossip and speculation. But we would like to be focused on the race, on the performance, on the team, on Fred," Conti added.

"The storm of communication around the team -- we are used to that, Ferrari is used to that.

"With more than 21 social media channels covering all the company, the fact is that after the race and on Sunday and yesterday, we can say this storm of communication was increasing. Normally it's going down.

"And as we have a race the next weekend in Malaysia, we would like to take the time to ask you kindly not to focus on this. Fred is in his position and we are confirming his leadership. And we would like to be focused on the race, the team and its leadership.

"This is why we have done it. Because looking and monitoring the communication yesterday, today, normally it's going down. But everybody, not just you guys, but also Italian media from all over the world, they are still creating a lot of different stories around Fred.

"And this is not useful. So this is why we decided to do that."

Vassuer has been Ferrari boss since 2023 and almost led the team to a constructors' championship the following season, narrowly missing out to McLaren. He played an instrumental role in signing Hamilton to the team at the start of 2025.

Ferrari started this season looking like the closest challengers to the dominant Mercedes team. Lewis Hamilton won in Spain before Charles Leclerc won in Great Britain, but the team's results have dried up recently. Ferrari has not been on the podium at any of the last five races.

stories.headline: Five stats: Why USMNT should be excited about Cavan Sullivan
stories.summary: Is the hype around Cavan Sullivan's USMNT future too much? No, it's actually not enough -- and here are five reasons why.
stories.body:
There's something incredible happening in MLS right now, and the average World Cup watcher probably has no clue.

Seriously, think about all of the people you know who are "sports fans" but maybe not "soccer fans" -- the ones who root hard for the U.S. men's national team every four years and know the names of their four or five best players.

Sure, they probably still can't pronounce the last name of manager Mauricio Pochettino, but they watched tons of soccer this summer. The World Cup had so many games, and finally, it was all aligned with our time zones. These people now have opinions about VAR, England's prevent defense and the general moral fiber of the Argentina national team.

They're primed to care about soccer, especially American soccer, and especially a kind of greatness we've never seen before from a player of a certain age. No, I'm not talking about Lionel Messi, who somehow (1) might still be the greatest soccer player in the world, (2) is easily the greatest 39-year-old soccer player we've ever seen, and (3) continues to play soccer every week, across North America, without having any effect on North American sports discourse.

No, I'm talking about Cavan Sullivan, the 16-year-old phenom who, somehow, still feels as if he's being underhyped.

The history of American soccer is filled with players who were overpromised and couldn't do anything but underdeliver, but this is different. It's not just that we, Americans, have never seen someone like Sullivan. No, the wider soccer world -- the rest of the entire world -- rarely ever sees someone like Sullivan.

Here are some numbers for why you should get excited:

1,675 minutes
As I like to often say: The best predictor of future stardom is minutes players at a young age.

Take the three front-runners for this year's Ballon d'Or. Harry Kane was playing and scoring goals for Millwall in the Championship during his age-18 season. Lamine Yamal is 19 -- right now. And Kylian Mbappé broke out for Monaco during his age-17 season.

Sullivan is currently in his age-16 season (defined by your age at the start of the campaign). And so far, he has played 1,675 league minutes in MLS.

The site FBref has data for what they call the "Next 14" -- essentially, the most competitive leagues in the world after Europe's Big Five -- that goes back to the beginning of the current century, if not more. Only 21 outfield players have played more league minutes than Sullivan, who still has at least eight games left in his season. If we expand the dataset to include the Big Five, then only five other players -- Eduardo Camavinga, Alex Song, Gavi, Lamine Yamal, and Nuri Sahin -- have played more minutes than Sullivan before their age-17 season.

The leader, among all of these players? Freddy Adu had played 5,448 minutes by the end of his age-16 season.

€1.54 billion
Though we don't have much useful leaguewide data dating to 2006, when Adu was wrapping up his age-16 season, I do feel confident in saying the following: MLS is a lot better than it was 20 years ago.

Heck, it's a lot better than it was even 10 years ago. Per a recent analysis by Michael Caley: In 2016, the average combined transfer value of the median MLS team (as estimated by the site Transfermarkt) was significantly lower than the average team in the first divisions in Mexico, Belgium, Portugal and the Netherlands. Since then, the league has essentially caught up to Belgium and Mexico in transfer value, and it has surpassed Portugal and the Netherlands.

Though the biggest teams in those European leagues are still way better and richer than any MLS side -- thanks to Champions League prize money -- the average match that Cavan Sullivan plays in MLS is probably tougher than what he'd face were he playing for Benfica, Porto or PSV.

All in all, the combined estimated transfer values of all 30 MLS clubs is €1.54 billion -- or about €51.3 million per team.

12 goals and assists
For the Big Five leagues, FBref has goal-and-assist data dating to at least the mid-1990s for Ligue 1, for the entirety of the Premier League since its breakaway from the English Football League in 1992, and the late 1980s for Italy, Germany and Spain.

Over that stretch, the record for goals+assists before a player's age-17 season comes from Bojan Krkic, who scored 10 goals and created three more in his early years -- right at the beginning of Pep Guardiola's dominance with Barcelona. Next after him is a tie between Yamal and Wayne Rooney's Everton years, at 10.

Sullivan currently has 12 -- a nearly even split between seven goals and five assists. If we expand the list out to the Next 14 leagues, then only four players have more. Chelsea's Estêvão registered 23 goal contributions with Palmeiras in Brazil's top flight -- a much tougher league than MLS. Normally, I'd remove penalties from the equation, but the fact that Estevao was chosen to take three penalties as a 16-year-old feels like useful information.

Then there's Adu with 22, Romelu Lukaku with 19 for Anderlecht, and Endrick's 15 with Palmeiras before he moved to Real Madrid.

The smart money is on Sullivan moving up the list over the next month as MLS wraps up its regular season. In his eight games since the World Cup, he has scored six goals and added four assists.

132 passes into the attacking third
Sullivan is the rare attacking prospect whose attacking production actually underrates his track record.

Of course, the production at this point in his career is fantastic -- bested only by a collection of some of the best attacking prospects of the past 30 years. But that production is backed up by a sustainable drumbeat of quality shots and chances created, plus a bedrock of excellent ball progression and off-ball movement.

To dig into some more advanced numbers, we need to move beyond FBref's historical database. Stats Perform doesn't have numbers that extend to the 1990s, but we're able to look at the Big Five in Europe, MLS, Liga MX, the Dutch Eredivisie, the English second division, a number of cup competitions in Europe and South America, plus the first divisions in Portugal, Brazil, Argentina and Colombia. The data dates to at least the mid-2010s.

Among all of the players who fall within there, Sullivan ranks third and second, respectively, in the two most important and predictive attacking metrics: expected goals and expected assists. The other players I've highlighted in the below chart, which only looks at minutes played at age 16 or earlier, mostly played in more difficult leagues, but across the modern era of the sport almost no one has done what Sullivan is currently doing, still eight years away from the start of his prime:

He's also not just standing up near the goal and waiting for things to happen. Among this same cohort, Sullivan leads all players in passes played into the attacking third, with 132. The only other players with more than 100 are Jude Bellingham (104) and Gilberto Mora (109), both of whom are midfielders, not attackers.

That's clear when we look at passes played into the penalty area. Both Mora and Bellingham landed right around 100; Sullivan is all the way up at 202. Only Yamal, at 254, played more.

Scoring goals, creating chances, moving the ball into the attacking third, moving the ball into the box -- that's all there. The only thing missing is an ability to find space off of the ball, and it's only missing because I haven't mentioned it yet.

Sullivan has taken 142 touches inside the box. Among this cohort, Yamal, again, is the only player with more.

78 rating
The best players in modern soccer are the wide attackers who score goals, create chances, move the ball into attacking positions and find space inside the box. The best attacking prospects -- players in their late teens and early 20s -- tend to be able to score and create goals at a young age, but that's it. They usually can't aid in buildup play -- outside of slowing things down with a succession of head-down dribbles that sometimes move the ball upfield but often kill attacks by allowing the defense to recover. And they rarely have an advanced enough understanding of space and ball movement to be patient and savvy enough to receive passes in dangerous positions.

This all-conquering winger is a new prototype of player -- so new that the two best examples, Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo, are still playing. And so we haven't seen many young players develop with this idea in mind. That is, until Yamal -- and yes, now Sullivan.

The just-turned-17-year-old doesn't just have good-for-a-16-year-old numbers in his first real professional season. No, he genuinely has been one of the best players in MLS.

The player-rating model from the stats app Futi looks at how much every touch increases or decreases his team's chances of scoring and conceding a goal. Then it adjusts for the player's role and how well his team plays when he's on and off the field. And finally, they convert it all into an easy-to-understand 0-to-100 scale.

Among players with at least 1,500 minutes played this season, Sullivan currently ranks in the top 10 for the Futi model. The average age of the players ahead of him is nearly twice his: 31. And that's all for the full season; if we looked only at the post-World-Cup stretch, he probably would be even higher:

There are still plenty of questions.

Will he grow? What happens when he has moved beyond Philadelphia's relatively chaotic system? How might he handle moving and living in Europe? Those questions -- and more -- would hold true for any 16-year-old soccer player.

But while it probably won't happen because it's an unlikely outcome for everyone who has ever lived, Sullivan's early-career excellence means that he is more likely to become a superstar than any American who has come before him.

Just consider this. Futi also rates each individual area of a player's in-possession performance: shooting, creating, receiving, dribbling and linking (or buildup play). There are two players in the league who rate above a 60 in all five.

The two: Cavan Sullivan and Lionel Messi.

stories.headline: NRL Grand Final to honour retired Souths star
stories.summary: The NRL will honour retired South Sydney player Jai Arrow as part of the grand final pre-match entertainment, featuring the song "You'll Never Walk Alone" as he completes a lap of the field.
stories.body:
The NRL will honour retired South Sydney player Jai Arrow as part of the Grand Final prematch entertainment, featuring the song "You'll Never Walk Alone" as he completes a lap of the field.

A week after stating the NRL showpiece at Accor Stadium on Sunday night didn't need a headline act following a fall-out with artist Tones and I, NRL boss Peter V'landys confirmed to AAP there will now be a musical tribute involving Arrow.

The Rabbitohs favourite was forced into immediate retirement in May after being diagnosed with motor neurone disease (MND).

Since then, the game and wider sporting community has continued to honour the 31-year-old.

The song made famous by Gerry and the Pacemakers with a cover in the 1960s, and adopted by Liverpool FC as its official motto, has featured heavily across the tributes.

A group of Australian musicians will sing it from 7.05pm (AEDT), with the set lasting 11 minutes, before kick-off at 7.30pm.

V'landys' backflip followed public backlash over the decision to go without any musical entertainment, with the wowing performance by Kylie Minogue at the AFL Grand Final fuelling the criticism.

The NRL boss insisted last week it was not an issue that the rugby league decider would go without, comparing the prematch entertainment to a pickle in a burger.

He instead pledged to spend $1 million on grassroots rugby league.

However V'Landys then changed his mind and teased the entertainment on Monday.

"I've got to tell you it'll be the highest-rating 11 minutes you will ever see, because no one knows what it is and we won't tell until the night," the newly-elevated executive chairman told reporters.

"And a lot of people will be surprised.

"There will be something, but I am not saying what it is. Stay tuned."

stories.headline: Padres pummel Cubs behind Tatis' leadoff blast, King's gem in Game 1
stories.summary: The Padres made an emphatic statement in their wild-card opener against the Cubs, getting a leadoff homer from Fernando Tatis Jr. and a brilliant effort on the mound from Michael King in an 8-0 win in Game 1.
stories.body:
SAN DIEGO -- Fernando Tatis Jr. hit the first leadoff homer in Padres playoff history on the Cubs' first pitch, Michael King took a no-hitter into the seventh inning and San Diego rolled to an 8-0 victory over Chicago in their National League Wild Card Series opener Tuesday night.

Manny Machado also homered in the first inning and added an RBI double in the third during an emphatic opening statement by the 91-win Padres. Xander Bogaerts also homered off Cubs starter Matthew Boyd, and Jackson Merrill added a two-run single later.

San Diego provided more than enough support for King, who struck out eight over seven stellar innings while thoroughly throttling the majors' highest-scoring team. King set the tone by striking out probable NL MVP Pete Crow-Armstrong with the game's first three pitches.

Nico Hoerner got the Cubs' only hit off King with a one-out infield single in the seventh, but King racked up two more strikeouts to earn the last of several standing ovations from the raucous sellout crowd watching his third career playoff start.

Game 2 is Wednesday night at Petco Park. The series winner faces the MLB-best Milwaukee Brewers in the best-of-five division series.

Chicago had just one hit before getting to Joe Musgrove, the Padres veteran making his first major league appearance since Oct. 2, 2024, in the ninth inning. The Cubs got two singles and a walk before Musgrove struck out pinch hitter Michael Conforto to preserve the shutout in his return from Tommy John surgery.

The Padres dominated the opener of this rematch of last fall's wild-card series, won by the Cubs in three tight games. San Diego scored more runs in the first five innings of this series opener than it did last year in all three games at Wrigley Field combined.

San Diego finished this season with the majors' sixth-best record, besting Chicago by two wins and setting franchise records with its third straight playoff berth and fifth straight winning record. The Padres hit the postseason on a 17-3 roll, and they're still surging.

Boyd's opening pitch was a changeup, and Tatis crushed it 405 feet to center in a blast reminiscent of his first-inning homer in Game 1 of San Diego's 2024 NL Wild Card Series victory over Atlanta.

Moments later, Machado smashed another changeup out to left-center, setting off pandemonium at Petco with his franchise-record ninth postseason homer.

Tatis walked in the third and scored from first on Machado's double to the wall. Bogaerts connected in the fourth, lining a full-count changeup into the seats on the Western Metal Supply Co. building above left field.

San Diego loaded the bases in the fifth against reliever Javier Assad, and Merrill cracked a two-run single to center before Ty France scored on a passed ball.

King escaped the minor trouble he faced, picking up key strikeouts and throwing his sweeper superbly. Hoerner got Chicago's hit on a grounder that Machado stopped with difficulty, but couldn't transfer to his throwing hand cleanly enough to make a play.

Tatis scored his third run in the seventh when he singled, stole second and ran all the way home when the throw trickled into center. Tatis slid headfirst past the tag and came up screaming while Machado theatrically signaled him safe.

Nick Pivetta (3-2, 2.86 ERA) starts Game 2 for the Padres in his fifth game back from a near five-month absence with a right elbow injury. Kevin Gausman (4-2, 4.83) goes for the Cubs.

stories.headline: Eichel hits 700 points as Golden Knights beat Blackhawks in Ryan Craig’s first game behind the bench
stories.summary: — Jack Eichel had a goal and two assists to reach 701 career points, and the Vegas Golden Knights beat the Chicago Blackhawks 5-2 in their season opener Tuesday night.
stories.body:
LAS VEGAS -- — Jack Eichel had a goal and two assists to reach 701 career points, and the Vegas Golden Knights beat the Chicago Blackhawks 5-2 in their season opener Tuesday night.


Victor Olofsson notched Vegas’ first goal of the season, rookie Trevor Connelly scored in his NHL debut and Noah Hanifin and Mark Stone added goals as Ryan Craig earned his first victory as the Golden Knights’ head coach. Carter Hart made 24 saves.


Jordan Greenway and Patrick Kane scored for Chicago, and Spencer Knight stopped 32 shots.


Kane marked his return to the franchise he helped lead to three Stanley Cup championships with a third-period goal, but Chicago couldn’t complete the comeback.


Craig took over after six seasons as a Vegas assistant and three coaching its AHL affiliate in Henderson. He inherited a veteran team that reached last season’s Stanley Cup Final.


Vegas got scoring from five players after trading Pavel Dorofeyev, its leading goal scorer last season with 37, including 20 on the man advantage.


Olofsson opened the scoring midway through the first period when his power-play wrist shot found the top shelf from the far side.


Connelly doubled the lead when he flipped a rebound over Knight’s pads.


Greenway scored late in the second when his shot from the right circle flew past Hart, cutting Vegas’ lead to 2-1.


Kane trimmed the deficit to one early in the third with a slick backhand, but Hanifin answered shortly thereafter to restore the two-goal cushion.


Stone’s empty-netter provided the final margin.


Chicago opened without Connor Bedard, who is recovering from shoulder surgery and isn’t expected back until late October at the earliest.


Up next
Blackhawks: Visit Utah on Thursday night.


Golden Knights: Host Anaheim on Friday night.
